script.stored_text_completeness: All 18536 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("that fight is worth winning."); ASR artifacts ("Not 80,000.8.", "Twothirds", "SNP 500", "soarses"); the savings-rate and renter-difficulty passages are repeated; fillers ("Um", "Uh"); 3,167 words over 1,259 seconds (~151 wpm) is consistent with a full read; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: The median bank account balance in America is $8,000. Not 80,000.8. If you have more than that sitting in your checking or savings account right now, you are statistically wealthier than half the country. Let that sink in for a second. Half of all American households have less than 8 grand to their name in liquid savings. And yet, um, you know what's wild? The economy is supposedly doing great. The stock market hit record highs in 2025. Unemployment is
script.ending_words: sitting here realizing you're behind the median or worse, way behind, don't spiral. The averages are broken. The system is extracting, but you're not powerless. Start small. Track the gap. Build the margin. And stop comparing yourself to people whose wealth came from timing and luck you didn't have. You're not in a race against them. You're in a fight for your own stability, and that fight is worth winning.
script.analysis: Full 18536 canonical characters read. A statistics roundup with a "split-screen economy" thesis: median bank balance, paycheck-to-paycheck share, emergency and retirement savings gaps, inflation vs wages, pessimism, wealth and retirement magic numbers, retirement medians by age, a 4% example with Social Security, generational debt, credit cards, savings rate, renting and mortgage costs, a card-payoff example, a millennial debt-service example, asset-owner vs wage-earner divergence, and a self-comparison close. Verified: Northwestern Mutual 2025 $1.26M; mortgage P&I and rent-share arithmetic reproduce. Wrong or stale: card payoff (137 months/$12,150, not 94/$6,160), wages "maybe 10%" vs ~28-30% nominal growth, median household income $75,000 (stale), 54% with no retirement savings (unsourced, high). Savings-rate and renter passages repeat. The stored ending is complete.
